prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [adversarial] Long headers over tiny numbers (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Site" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 2: header "Average weekly active users across all platforms" · longest unbreakable word 70px · one-line width 347px
  col 3: header "Median session length in minutes" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 238px
  col 4: header "Share of sessions that ended in a purchase" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 307px
  col 5: header "Number of support tickets opened" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 246px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare site-level activity, session behavior, purchase conversion, and support demand across three sites.","reading":"Readers scan across each site’s row to see its profile and down each metric column to compare sites. The headers carry much more text than the values, so their wrapping will largely determine header height.","groups":["Columns 2–5 are comparable site metrics and should have a consistent visual rhythm.","Columns 3 and 4 both describe session behavior; column 2 measures audience activity and column 5 measures support demand."],"keep_intact":["Site identifiers and numeric values, including decimals and abbreviations.","Individual words in the headers."],"may_wrap":["The four descriptive metric headers can wrap at word boundaries. Their shared header row can absorb multiple lines without increasing the height of individual data rows."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [55, 180, 145, 175, 164] · table 720×193px · row heights [83, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [55, 170, 145, 190, 159] · table 720×193px · row heights [83, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [55, 195, 145, 165, 159] · table 720×193px · row heights [83, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
